course_description.character: The 2027 Gran Fondo is a 119km point-to-point road route with 3,300m of climbing, starting at the Cenes de la Vega municipal sports center and finishing at Pradollano ski station at approximately 2,100m altitude. It is not the separate 38km Subida al Veleta held the following day. The current course page identifies two crossings of Puerto de Blancares and a late 15km timed ascent from Maitena through El Duque and La Sabina. Its climb table has not been fully cleaned for 2027: the El Duque and La Sabina kilometre markers run beyond the stated 119km finish, and the page's download button currently serves an unrelated HUEX Gran Fondo GPX. Those stale artifacts are not treated as 2027 route facts.
course_description.signature_challenge: The official 15km no-drafting timed ascent packs 1,177m of climbing into the final mountain phase after riders have already accumulated two crossings of Puerto de Blancares.
suffering_zones: Puerto de Blancares from Quéntar — 7.3km on the current organizer climb table, arriving before the first listed aid point
Puerto de Blancares from La Peza — 9.4km from the opposite side before the route reaches Güéjar Sierra
Maitena-El Duque-La Sabina — the 15km, 1,177m no-drafting timed ascent that defines the late race

logistics.lodging_strategy: Collaborations with TODOSIERRANEVADA for discounts; Granada city offers charming hotels minutes away.
logistics.transport: Bib pickup is at the Cenes de la Vega municipal sports center Friday 17:00-21:00 or race morning 07:00-07:45. A start-line bag drop transfers belongings to Pradollano. The organizer describes the self-return as 25km of almost continuous descent with 1,454m of elevation loss; riders not descending by bike need their own transfer plan.

history.origin_story: Emblematic Spanish gran fondo showcasing Granada's cycling heritage with Gran Fondo and Subida al Veleta formats.

biased_opinion.verdict: Dense, Legitimate Climbing — With a Sloppy Route Page
biased_opinion.summary: Sierra Nevada Límite is confirmed for 15 May 2027 with registration open: 119km, 3,300m of climbing, an 08:00 Cenes de la Vega start, and a Pradollano finish around 2,100m. That is a serious amount of vertical for a 119km road day, and the organizer adds a 15km, 1,177m no-drafting timed ascent late in the route. The operational page is detailed enough to plan aid and cutoff timing, but it also retains climb kilometre markers beyond the finish and links its GPX button to an unrelated HUEX course. Use the published race vitals and named challenges; wait for a corrected GPX before locking recon or pacing to exact kilometres.
strengths: Exceptional climbing density — 3,300m across 119km is a genuinely hard ratio
Authentic Sierra Nevada high-mountain roads with a Pradollano ski-station finish around 2,100 m
Four listed on-course aid points, a bag transfer, checkpoint closures, and finish food give riders a concrete support plan
Two sides of Puerto de Blancares lead into a distinct 15km timed mountain sector
weaknesses: The current climb table puts El Duque and La Sabina beyond the stated 119km finish, so those kilometre labels are stale
The official GPX button currently downloads a HUEX Gran Fondo route in another part of Spain, not Sierra Nevada
The regulations page still names the 2026 date even though the event page and registration system are current for 2027
This Gran Fondo finishes at Pradollano, not the Veleta summit; Subida al Veleta is a separate event the next day
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A legitimately hard and now-confirmed 2027 climbing test. Build for 119km and 3,300m, but do not trust the downloadable track until the organizer replaces the unrelated GPX.

final_verdict.one_liner: A short, brutally vertical Sierra Nevada fondo with a real 2027 date and a route page that still needs cleanup.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want 3,300m of climbing in a compact 119km day and a timed late ascent. Confirm the corrected GPX before race week, and do not confuse the Pradollano finish with the separate Veleta event.
final_verdict.alternatives: For the actual Veleta summit ascent, ride the Subida al Veleta (same organizer, the following day). For a comparably dense Spanish climbing fondo, look at other high-Sierra or Pyrenees gran fondos.
